ingredients.item: /4 tsp ground ginger , plus 1 tbsp fresh grated ginger
rice wine or soju — the traditional tenderizer
toasted sesame seeds , optional, in the dough
About 60 g additional flour, for the board and stamp
About 800 ml neutral oil, for the two-stage fry

instructions.heading: Roll thick, cut, and stamp
instructions.action: Roll thick, cut, and stamp. The dough rolled between floured parchment to 1 cm — thick, by cookie standards — and cut into shapes: the traditional flower stamp pressed into rounds, or simple diamonds for the honest home version. Dock each cookie twice with a fork (steam vents — the fry puffs them) and rest the cut cookies 15 minutes while the oil heats.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: each cut cookie holds its edge cleanly; a ragged edge means the dough warmed too much — back to the fridge for ten minutes.

instructions.heading: The two-stage fry — infuse, then color
instructions.action: The two-stage fry — infuse, then color. Stage one: oil at 130 °C (gentle — a cookie dropped in takes 4–5 seconds to bubble to the surface), the cookies in small batches, 12–15 minutes, turned once — they barely color, and the low heat cooks the starch through while the sesame oil's flavor soaks the interior. Stage two: the oil raised to 170 °C, the same cookies returned for 90 seconds — they turn deep gold-brown and the surface crisps.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: stage one's cookie is pale-blond and cooked through (break one: no raw dough at the center), and stage two's is golden with a light crust and a delicate, almost pastry-flaky interior. The double fry exists because a single hot fry colors the outside long before the honey-laden interior cooks — the honey burns, the center stays raw — and there is no single-temperature workaround.

instructions.heading: The syrup bath — while hot
instructions.action: The syrup bath — while hot. The simmered syrup taken off the heat, and the hot-from-the-oil cookies slid straight in, 30–60 seconds a side, then lifted to a rack over a tray. They drink the syrup as they cool, turning from golden to translucent amber, the surface going glassy.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the cooled cookie's test: glossy, translucent at the edges, tender-firm, the ginger-honey flavor soaked fully through — the first bite should explain the "medicine" in the name to anyone who thinks it a metaphor. A syrup-bathed yakgwa keeps three weeks and is best at days 2–5.

visualDonenessCues: The dough: minimally mixed, rested an hour, rolled thick, docked twice.
The fry: stage one 130 °C to cooked-through-and-pale, stage two 170 °C to golden in 90 seconds.
The syrup: simmered with ginger, the hot cookies bathed as they leave the oil.
The finish: cooled to translucent-amber, glossy, tender-firm; best at days 2–5 of three weeks.
storageNotes: The keeper of the dessert list: three weeks airtight, improving through the first five days as the syrup soaks. Make a double batch when the honey jar is generous.

Variations: pressed with a pine-nut half before frying; a cinnamon thread in the syrup; the temple-style thick diamond, cut 2 cm and fried longer at the low stage — chewier, the meditation-hall register.
